To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a dominant selective pressure on coding-sequence divergence across metazoan lineages is mistranslation-induced protein misfolding, 2) the mechanistic model of evolution that emerges is testable and has implications for the interpretation of molecular evolution data and for neurodegenerative diseases, and 3) the model suggests that the Ka/Ks ratio, the ratio of nonsynonymous to synonymous substitutions per site, should not be used to detect functional selection.
